issues.legal_issue: The relevant time for determining whether any claimant has taken possession in a disputed succession proceeding for appointment of an estate administrator is the commencement of the proceeding.
material_facts: Several claimants disputed succession to an estate that had been in the deceased widow’s exclusive possession until her death.
The court found that none of the claimants was in possession when the proceedings under the Regulation commenced.
The claimant’s revenue entry and rent notes evidencing possession were obtained after the proceedings commenced.
issues.conclusion: The possession requirement was satisfied because no claimant was in possession when the proceedings commenced; possession obtained afterward did not alter that result, and appointment of an administrator was justified.
issues.legal_principle: Under the relevant clause of rule 9 of the Bombay Regulation VIII of 1827, possession is assessed as of the commencement of the proceedings, whether they begin on a claimant’s application or suo motu. The preamble’s purpose of providing for orderly management and devolution of an estate supports this construction. Rules 8 and 9 show that the resulting decision is summary and does not finally determine title, which remains for a competent civil court.

predicates.disputed_estate_management_proceeding: A proceeding was brought to arrange management of an estate while entitlement to succeed to it remained unresolved.
predicates.succession_rights_are_contested: Two or more claimants disputed who was entitled to succeed to the estate.
predicates.no_claimant_in_possession_at_commencemen: No claimant was in possession of the estate when the management proceeding began.

issues.definition: When an estate-management proceeding concerns contested succession and no claimant possessed the estate when the proceeding began, an interim administrator’s appointment is justified.
